text: What is a critical incident response team? Jefferson County CIRT in Colorado. A critical incident response team is a group of investigators that examines a serious event involving police, such as an officer-involved shooting. The Jefferson County Critical Incident Response Team is the group assigned to investigate the Lakewood, Colorado, bus shooting in which one officer died and three were wounded.. One Lakewood, Colorado, police officer was killed and three others were wounded in a gunfight with a suspect who tried to board an RTD bus on Thursday night. The Jefferson County Critical Incident Response Team was named to investigate the shooting.. The shooting took place on a Thursday evening in Lakewood, a suburb about 5 miles west of downtown Denver. Officers were called to the area of Colfax and Wadsworth around 6:30 p.m. After a report of a suspicious person who might have been tied to an earlier hit-and-run. The suspect was trying to board a Regional Transportation District bus on Route 76 when officers reached him. Lakewood Police spokesman John Romero said the suspect opened fire within seconds, and the suspect was killed in the gunfire. A civilian was also injured, and the circumstances of that injury were not yet clear. Romero said the Jefferson County team would conduct the inquiry into the shooting. Its role is to look at the facts of the encounter from outside the agency involved, so that the department is not investigating its own officers alone. The identities of the officers and the suspect had not been released at the time of the press conference. The case matters now because it is one of the most serious losses in the Lakewood Police Department's recent history, with one officer killed and three others wounded. Colorado Gov. Jared Polis said in a statement that he was heartbroken by the death. The bus operator, RTD, said its thoughts were with those affected and that the safety of its riders and employees remained its highest priority.
